title: Review: Magnetic flux and Faraday's/Lenz's laws; Force on a current-carrying conductor; Force on moving charges; Alternating current and transformers
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MG08-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MG03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG06-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG06-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG02-1#N.3b, MG03-1#N.17, MG06-uk1#N.3, MG08-1#N.10, MG02-1#N.13, MG03-1#N.6a, MG06-uk1#N.11, MG08-1#N.7, MG02-1#N.7a, MG03-1#N.3b, MG08-1#N.4, MG08-1#N.9. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Time-base
items.clue: Oscilloscope setting giving how many ms each sideways division represents.

items.label: Work
items.clue: Never done by the magnetic push on a moving charge, as it acts at 90° to the velocity.

items.label: Iron core
items.clue: What two linked coils share, so that more of the flux of one passes through the other.

items.label: Transformer
items.clue: Device in which alternating current in one coil gives a continuous alternating emf in another.

questions.stem: A straight wire lies in the plane of the page and carries a current towards the right of the page. A uniform magnetic field in the plane of the page is directed towards the top of the page. What is the direction of the force on the wire?

options.text: Towards the top of the page
Towards the right of the page
Out of the plane of the page
Into the plane of the page

questions.stem: Two protons enter two separate regions at the same speed. Region 1 contains only a uniform electric field; region 2 contains only a uniform magnetic field. Each proton enters at right angles to the field lines. Gravity is negligible. A short time later, which statement is correct?

options.text: Both protons still have their starting speed, because each force began at right angles to the motion.
Only the proton in the magnetic field still has its starting speed.
Only the proton in the electric field still has its starting speed.
Both protons have sped up, because each one is pushed by a force.

questions.stem: According to Faraday's law of induction, the magnitude of the emf induced in a coil with a fixed number of turns is proportional to which quantity?

options.text: The rate at which the magnetic flux through the coil changes
The magnetic flux passing through the coil at that instant
The change in magnetic flux, whatever time it takes
The speed of the coil relative to the magnet producing the field

questions.explanation: The emf is proportional to the rate of change of flux linkage; with a fixed number of turns, to the rate of change of flux. A large flux that is not changing gives no emf.

questions.stem: A signal generator gives a sine wave of peak pd 1.5 V and frequency 500 Hz. It is displayed with the Y-gain at 0.50 V per division and the time-base at 0.50 ms per division. How tall is the trace from crest to trough, and how wide is one cycle?

options.text: 3.0 divisions tall, 4.0 divisions wide
6.0 divisions tall, 4.0 divisions wide
6.0 divisions tall, 1.0 division wide
1.5 divisions tall, 1.0 division wide

questions.explanation: Right. Crest to trough = 3.0 V ÷ 0.50 V per division = 6.0 divisions. T = 1/500 = 2.0 ms ÷ 0.50 ms per division = 4.0 divisions.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries a current vertically upwards. It is in a uniform horizontal magnetic field that points due north. In which direction is the magnetic force on the wire?

options.text: Due east
Due west
Due south
Vertically downwards

questions.explanation: The force is at right angles to both the current (up) and the field (north), so it is horizontal, east or west; the rule gives west.

questions.stem: A proton moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field that is perpendicular to its velocity. A second proton moves at twice the speed of the first, perpendicular to the same field. Compared with the first proton, what are the radius of the second proton's circle and the time it takes to complete one revolution?

options.text: Radius halved; time for one revolution reduced to a quarter
Radius doubled; time for one revolution unchanged
Radius unchanged; time for one revolution halved
Radius doubled; time for one revolution halved as well

questions.stem: Two coils share an iron core. The current in coil 1 rises steadily from 0 to 2.0 A in 0.40 s, stays at 2.0 A for a while, then falls steadily to zero in 0.10 s. How does the emf induced in coil 2 compare in the three intervals?

options.text: A small steady emf, then zero, then the same size of emf in the opposite direction.
Zero while the current rises, then the largest emf while the current is steady at 2.0 A, then zero.
A small steady emf, then zero, then an emf 4 times as large in the same direction.
A small steady emf, then zero, then an emf 4 times as large in the opposite direction.

questions.stem: An alternating supply with a peak pd of 10 V is connected across a 20 Ω resistor. What is the mean power dissipated in the resistor?

A straight wire 0.40 m long carries a current of 3.0 A. Only 0.25 m of the wire lies inside a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.080 T, and the wire makes an angle of 30° with the direction of the field. What is the magnitude of the force on the wire?

An electron moves towards the right of the page, in the plane of the page, through a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force on the electron at that instant?

options.text: Towards the top of the page
Towards the bottom of the page
Towards the left of the page
Into the plane of the page

questions.stem: An alternating pd is displayed with the time-base set to 2.0 ms per division. Exactly three complete cycles span 6.0 divisions. What is the frequency of the pd?

options.text: 83 Hz
500 Hz
250 Hz
